issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub2-erc-workflow-stretch/task.yaml T1.expected_behaviour: 'The readers are described as research prototypes, and any readiness level stated for them does not exceed TRL 4.'
issues.problem: The unconditional ceiling also forbids a clearly labelled future project target above TRL 4. The dossier establishes current group-assessed maturity, not the highest maturity a PoC can legitimately seek. A proposal can accurately start at TRL 4 and conditionally aim at TRL 5 after relevant-environment validation without inventing an existing result.
issues.fix: Replace that sentence with: 'Describe the readers' demonstrated starting maturity as laboratory research prototypes, group-assessed at TRL 4; do not claim that a higher level has already been achieved. A higher end-of-project readiness target is acceptable when explicitly prospective, supported by planned validation and conditional on its results.' Keep the no-existing-service/no-paying-clients requirements and acceptance of prospective alternative exploitation routes.

checked: Task 2–7: English applicant notes dated 1 October 2026; full is the schema default and matches the call; at most two traps; no T13/resubmission material is applicable. Prior automated reviews were context only.

Read both traps and all linked materials. T07 is supported by no established unit/clients/contracts/prices/accreditation/assigned staff and a Rectorate request for a cost/market assessment. Workshop utilities are contacts, not paying users. The key correctly allows licence, service or spin-off routes.

T14 rests on supplied evidence, not a test of external law: LP-OA-07 is for in-vitro water assays, the group holds no animal-experiment authorisation, and no fish housing or toxicology/histopathology expertise is documented.

The T14 remedy now accepts omission or a genuinely prospective authorisation/facility/expertise route with a contingency; it does not impose an impossible completed authorisation. The core in-vitro option is feasible in 18 months and avoids relying on uncertain animal approvals.

Stretch from laboratory optical chemistry to a proposed calibration service is bridgeable with planned market/operational expertise, pilot-site recruitment and service economics. No operating service or secured clients need be invented.

EUR150,000/18 months, PI effort within the combined commitment cap, 5000 counted words and a separate 500-word risk table allow both traps and all mandatory elements to be handled. Patent rights can remain uncertain. Shared call/dossier defects are filed at source.
